name: Require a second verification step at sign-in, so a stolen password alone is not enough
priorityReason: A password reaching the wrong person is the commonest breach, and nothing else stands behind it.

goal.actor: a Super Admin and every user
goal.capability: to require a second step at sign-in on the roles and people that need it
goal.outcome: a stolen password alone does not get anybody in

secondaryActors.involvement: Enrols their second factor, and may turn it on or off for themselves where it has not been enforced on them.

additional.description: A user signs in to an account where a second factor applies (BR-4).
A user has lost their second factor and asks the Super Admin to recover it (BR-6).

preconditions.condition: The user holds a generated account and has set their own password.
An authenticated session exists for enrolment.
Enforcing on a role or an individual requires the Super Admin (BR-1).

postConditions: Where the Super Admin enforced it on a role or a named individual, those users cannot turn it off.
Where it was not enforced, the user could enable or disable it themselves from their own profile.
The user enrolled their second factor.
At sign-in they entered their password and then the second factor.
Access was granted only where both succeeded, so a stolen password alone was not enough.
A lost factor was recovered by the Super Admin, and by nobody else.
Every enforcement, enrolment, and recovery is on the audit trail.

permissions.notes: Enforces multi-factor on chosen roles or on named individuals, and recovers a lost factor (BR-1, BR-6).
Enrols their second factor, and may turn it on or off for themselves where it has not been enforced on them (BR-2).

permissions.rowScope: No authority over anybody else's second factor. Recovery is the Super Admin's alone.

businessRules.rule: The Super Admin can enforce multi-factor authentication on a role or on a named individual. Where it is enforced, that user cannot turn it off.
Where the Super Admin has not enforced it, the user may enable or disable it themselves from their own profile.
The user enrols their own second factor. Nobody enrols one on their behalf.
At sign-in they enter their password, then the second factor.
Access is granted only when both succeed. A password alone grants nothing where a second factor applies, which is the whole point.
Recovery is handled by the Super Admin if the factor is lost. Nobody else can reset another person's factor, and the Super Admin records why.
Every enforcement, enrolment and recovery is written to the audit trail.
A user on whom it is enforced but who has not yet enrolled is held at enrolment on their next sign-in, and reaches nothing else until they have.
Removing enforcement does not remove an enrolled factor. The user keeps it unless they disable it themselves.
A failed second factor does not reveal whether the password was correct, since together they are one step.
A recovery resets the factor rather than bypassing it. The user enrols again.

transitions.condition: Multi-factor is enforced on the user's role or on them (BR-1, BR-8).
They enable it themselves and enrol (BR-2, BR-3).
They enrol at their next sign-in (BR-8).
The factor is lost and the Super Admin recovers it, with a reason (BR-6, BR-11).
They disable it, which is possible only where it is not enforced (BR-1, BR-2).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Settings → Multi-factor enforcement → Enforce on a role
basicFlow.userAction: Enforces multi-factor authentication on a role or on a named individual.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the enforcement. Those users cannot turn it off.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Account → My security → Enable multi-factor
basicFlow.userAction: Turns it on for themselves, where the Super Admin has not enforced it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Offers the setting only where it is not enforced.

basicFlow.userAction: Enrols their second factor and confirms it with a code.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Enrols it against their own account. Nobody enrols on their behalf.
Takes them to the second factor rather than into the system.
Grants access only where both the password and the factor succeeded.

basicFlow.navigation: Settings → Multi-factor enforcement → Recover a factor
basicFlow.userAction: Recovers a lost factor, with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Resets the factor rather than bypassing it. The user enrols again.
Writes every enforcement, enrolment and recovery to the audit trail.

alternateFlows.condition: The user is enforced but has not enrolled
alternateFlows.navigation: Sign in → Enrol your second factor
alternateFlows.behaviour: They are held at enrolment on their next sign-in and reach nothing else until they have enrolled (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: Multi-factor is enforced on the user
alternateFlows.behaviour: The disable control is not offered. Where it is enforced, the user cannot turn it off (BR-1).
Access is refused, and the message does not reveal whether the password was correct, since together they are one step (BR-5, BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The user has lost their factor
alternateFlows.navigation: Settings → Multi-factor enforcement → Recover a factor
alternateFlows.behaviour: The Super Admin resets it with a reason and the user enrols again. Nobody else can reset another person's factor (BR-6, BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: Enforcement is removed from a role
alternateFlows.behaviour: The users keep their enrolled factors unless they disable them themselves (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The user enrols by SMS rather than an authenticator
alternateFlows.navigation: Enrol your second factor → Method → SMS
alternateFlows.behaviour: The factor is sent to the number recorded against their record (BR-3).

exceptions.condition: The user attempts to disable an enforced factor
exceptions.messageShown: Multi-factor authentication is required for your role and cannot be turned off.

exceptions.condition: The confirming code does not match at enrolment

exceptions.condition: The message reveals that the password was correct
exceptions.systemResponse: It does not. The two are one step (BR-10).

exceptions.condition: The user has a password but no enrolled factor and is enforced
exceptions.messageShown: Enrol your second factor before continuing.

exceptions.condition: A School Admin attempts to recover somebody's factor
exceptions.messageShown: Only the Super Admin can recover a second factor.

exceptions.condition: A recovery is recorded with no reason
exceptions.messageShown: Give a reason for recovering this factor.

exceptions.condition: A recovery bypasses the factor rather than resetting it
exceptions.systemResponse: There is no such route. The user enrols again (BR-11).

exceptions.condition: The SMS method is chosen and no number is recorded
exceptions.messageShown: No contact number is recorded against your record.

departures.requirement: Where a second factor applies, no route grants access on the password alone.

departures.aspect: Enforcement cannot be turned off by its subject
departures.requirement: A user on whom it is enforced has no control anywhere that disables it.
A failed sign-in returns the same message whichever step failed.

Enforcements, enrolments and recoveries are retained 7 years.

openQuestions.question: Which roles does the school intend to enforce it on? Accounts and the Super Admin are the obvious ones and neither is stated.
openQuestions.assumption: Configurable. The school's choice is not stated.

openQuestions.question: Is a second factor sensible for guardians and students, or only for staff?
openQuestions.assumption: Available to all as modelled. Enforcing it on families would be a support burden.

openQuestions.question: Who recovers the Super Admin's own factor, given only the Super Admin recovers factors?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and it is the case that locks the school out.

openQuestions.question: Are recovery codes offered as a fallback, so a lost handset does not require the Super Admin?
Is a factor remembered on a trusted device, or required at every sign-in?

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
